Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: one complete five-view spacecraft design sheet for a new REGULAR Bounty Hunter freighter in the visual language of Freelancer (2003). It must look like a manufactured sibling of the BH fighter / Barracuda / Hammerhead family, with genuine compact freighter cargo volume. This is a new member of that family, NOT a pirate conversion. Study the references instead of substituting a generic science-fiction ship.

REFERENCE AUTHORITY, in supplied order:
1. Native BH ELITE cockpit close-ups: IMMUTABLE cabin authority. Preserve that exact rounded enclosing shell, framing and three panes, its original small size, and its upright forward-facing placement. This is the existing BH adaptation of the Liberty freighter cabin.
2. Native BH ELITE six views: identity, colour, forebody, dorsal/ventral fins, forward-reaching side-wing tips, and two vertically arranged rear engines.
3. Native LI FREIGHTER six views: PRIMARY FREIGHTER STRUCTURAL precedent. Read its modest front cabin, long cargo middle, substantial transverse hull collars, articulated changes of section, and tapered stern. It is a cargo craft, not a scaled-up fighter. Borrow this understanding, not its exact body.
4. Original LI freighter design sketch: PRIMARY support for the design of coherent large cargo planes, collar sections, recessed side fields and stern taper. Its old rectangular cockpit is NOT an allowed substitute for reference 1. Its side fan is not mandatory.
5. Native regular BW FREIGHTER: SECONDARY precedent for compact useful cargo volume, integrated cheeks, restrained wing size and functional engine support. Do not copy its pointed nose, cabin, three-engine triangle, or a pirate reskin.
Only the named structural idea below is the new variant; do not blend all cargo schemes into one overstuffed ship.

CABIN MUST STAY NATIVE BH:
At the forward tip is the exact compact rounded BH nose cabin. It has one broad shield/teardrop-shaped central pane wrapping up onto its rounded crown, plus an oval side pane on each side, divided by the original narrow solid frames. Retain the enclosing forehead, side shell and immediate chin. No new crossbars, added panes, cockpit growth, angular fighter canopy, flat windshield, long spear nose, or new pointed prow ahead of the glass. Glass dimensions are only about 2.45 wide x 1.93 high x 2.00 long in a ship roughly 24-29 units long: this is a small single-pilot cabin, never a large bridge. Grow cargo volume behind it. Preserve the whole cabin, not merely three blue shapes.

BH FORM LANGUAGE:
A bilaterally symmetric design with a vertically composed central body and recognizable rounded blunt head. A strong longitudinal shoulder/belt leads aft from the cabin; angular cargo planes have purposeful section changes and connected supports. Keep a distinct moderately sized dorsal fin and a compact ventral keel/fin. The dorsal fin is a broad flat tapering BH plate, not a thin antenna, horn or giant sail. Short side wings have forward-reaching pointed outer ends and visible moving-part seams. Exactly TWO functional rear-facing engines, one ABOVE the other on the centre plane, with the lower exhaust modestly forward of the upper exhaust, in the BH manner. Engines have actual recessed exhaust mouths; no extra side engines. Keep equipment pads modest. No weapons or projecting gun barrels.

CARGO AND MECHANICAL PLAUSIBILITY:
The body must enclose real cargo space, not merely giant fins surrounding an unchanged fighter core. Compact player freighter, not a capital ship. The complete cabin remains small and visibly separate from the cargo-body mass. Two adjacent roof hatch leaves open outward/upward; draw them CLOSED in all views and leave their future sweep clear. Hatch is a useful bounded roof section, not the entire roof. Dorsal fin and its receiving pocket are structurally separate from this hatch, normally ahead of it. Native BH side-wing concept folds DOWN and translates slightly aft/up into side clearance; preserve a seam and empty sweep region so no wing rotates through a solid cargo wall. Keep engines on fixed hull structure, not attached to folding tips. Depict flight configuration with wings and fin extended. Do not add impossible folding arrows: this is a shape study, not a validated kinematic drawing.

MATERIALS AND DETAIL:
Regular BH production finish: cool pale grey and muted blue-green structural belts, dark engine metal, dark teal glazing, sparse yellow-black equipment warnings. Same general panel language as Liberty, with medium-scale fitted panels, inset grilles and a few stepped mechanical joints. Liberty capital-ship panel fields or ventilation motifs may enrich larger surfaces, at player-ship scale. Clean maintained working craft with subtle wear, no pirate markings, patchwork donor plating, red rust blanket, skulls or spikes. Use geometric complexity in silhouette, section changes, depth and connected transitions, not hundreds of tiny greebles. No external pipes, cable bundles, decorative frames, open trusses, cages, rivet carpets, cathedral decoration, oversized emblems or rows of passenger windows. Closed structural surfaces and backed recesses. Moderate detail, comparable to the originals but clearly resolved.

PRESENTATION:
Landscape 3:2 concept sheet on light neutral warm-grey background, controlled studio lighting, crisply shaded hard-surface illustration with visible shape and gentle material texture. Upper half: LARGE FULL FRONT 3/4 on left and LARGE FULL REAR 3/4 on right. Both show the WHOLE SHIP within margins, including cabin, both wing-tip extents, fins, belly and engines. Lower row: SIDE, true overhead TOP, and straight REAR. Five depictions must describe one coherent ship with identical proportions and cabin, same fin positions and two-engine count. Keep all outline details readable; no scenery, perspective crop, isolated tail, humans, floating components, explosion or text paragraphs. Original native cockpit and full front/rear design outrank small labels.

PRIMARY SHAPE EXPERIMENT: LONG SECTIONAL HULL WITH TWO SOLID COLLARS.
Use LI freighter's longitudinal architecture most directly. The small blunt BH cabin sits at the front of a short narrower forebody. Behind it is a long, comparatively narrow, straight-sided cargo middle with chamfered upper edges and a deep faceted belly. Two thick transverse shell collars at the forward and aft ends of that cargo section create visible steps in SIDE and TOP. They are part of the closed hull, never hoops or frames with empty space. Between them, each flank has ONE long shallow backed rectangular-trapezoid panel field. The stern contracts markedly to a narrow engine housing with the two BH nozzles stacked vertically. Keep a restrained BH dorsal fin on the FORWARD collar ahead of the hatch, and a short lower keel terminating near the lower engine. Two modest forward-swept foldable wings attach low near the middle. Total length about three times maximum rigid body width. Side silhouette should read: small blunt head -> raised front collar -> long level cargo deck -> aft collar -> tapered short tail. This is a deliberate elongated freighter with rhythm of large sections.
